source.title: ORCAS-I: Queries Annotated with Intent using Weak Supervision
source.authors: Daria Alexander; Wojciech Kusa; A. D. de Vries

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: The study trains classifiers on Snorkel-generated weak labels and compares their performance with the weak-labeling classifier on a manually annotated test set. This is a conceptual comparison, not the original weak-model-to-strong-model setup or PGR measure.
record.gate_note: The reported benchmark-model and Snorkel macro F1 comparisons bear on whether models trained from weak labels outperform their weak supervisor. Snorkel LabelModel versus MajorityLabelVoter results are comparisons of weak-label aggregation methods, not training changes to the student, so they are not recorded as rows. The paper also reports precision, recall, accuracy and per-category results; rows below retain the macro F1 comparisons from Tables 7 and 8 as the main metric.
record.test_reason: A new setting: pretrained BERT-base and xtremedistil are fine-tuned on labels from a rule-based Snorkel weak labeller. They are scored on 1,000 human-labelled queries against that same labeller. That bears on V1, whether the student beats its weak supervisor. No PGR or gold-trained ceiling is reported. The supervisor is a rule system, not a weaker model, and the paper is not framed as weak-to-strong.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is correct. The authors also frame the null result as expected for a student learning from one teacher without external knowledge. They suggest that short, ungrammatical queries limit the transformers.
record.recipe_differences: The supervisor is a rule-based Snorkel weak-labeling system, not a weaker pretrained model; benchmark classifiers are trained on its labels and evaluated against human annotations. The study does not calculate PGR or a true-label strong-model ceiling.
record.method_sensitivity: Scores vary with input features (query versus query + URL) and taxonomy granularity (three top-level categories versus the full taxonomy).

fits_no_version.finding: Students trained on query-only input, using labels from the full query+URL Snorkel, beat a URL-ablated Snorkel. The SVM, BERT and xtremedistil students do so on both taxonomies, and their recall is higher.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A student trained on labels from a supervisor with privileged features can outperform a version of that supervisor stripped of those features.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual International ACM SIGIR Conference on Research and Development in Information Retrieval (SIGIR '22)
record.problems: The student-supervisor comparison is not a weak-model/strong-model test and provides no PGR or true-label strong ceiling. The test set has 1,000 queries from one dataset; the text gives no error bars or significance statistics for the benchmark comparisons, although it states that none significantly outperforms Snorkel with query + URL features.
record.rows_left_out: Precision, recall, accuracy, per-category scores, and the Snorkel LabelModel versus MajorityLabelVoter comparison are omitted; the retained rows report the main macro F1 student-versus-Snorkel comparisons from Tables 7 and 8. Dataset label-distribution statistics and cited results are also omitted because they do not report the student-versus-supervisor outcome.

untested.parts: No PGR is computed. There is no strong ceiling trained on gold labels, and the supervisor is a rule-based labeller rather than a weaker model.
No student-side training change is tested.
There is no size or supervisor-strength sweep, and only one intent task.
No tests of exploitation, distribution shift or shared-error effects.

record.verdict_notes: The record's query-only comparisons misread the setup. Section 7.2 says the models learn from labels made by 'the Snorkel query and URL functions', so the query-only Snorkel is not the supervisor. Only the query+URL comparisons with pretrained students are kept for V1. Classical classifiers (logistic regression, SVM, fastText) are not 'strong models' in V1's sense. No significance statistics are given beyond the authors' statement.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test a weaker model supervising a strong pretrained model, does not report PGR, and does not establish a strong-model ceiling from true-label training.
No student-training change is tested for raising PGR.
No PGR sweep over model size, supervisor strength, or representations; only one query-intent task is studied.
No evaluation of exploiting supervisor blind spots, distribution shift in weak-to-strong performance, or shared student-supervisor errors.
No theory about when a student must beat its supervisor.
No vision or other non-language modality.

rows.subject: Logistic regression
rows.operation_detail: trained using query features and evaluated against manual labels
rows.note: The student was trained on the weakly labelled ORCAS-I-2M dataset.
rows.check: The baseline is wrong. The student was trained on labels from the full query+URL Snorkel; the query-only Snorkel is a URL-muted variant that did not produce the labels. The student also sees less input than the supervisor. Logistic regression is not a strong pretrained student.

rows.check: Logistic regression on tf-idf is not a strong model, so V1's strong-student premise does not apply. It scores .784, below the supervisor's .822.

relationships.condition: Pretrained transformer students (BERT-base, xtremedistil) fine-tuned on full query+URL Snorkel labels with query+URL input, for both the three-category and the full taxonomy
relationships.reason: Macro F1 is .826/.817 vs .822 and .774/.772 vs .770. The authors say none significantly outperforms Snorkel, so the gain over the supervisor is about zero.
relationships.display_finding: BERT-base and xtremedistil achieved macro F1 of 0.826 and 0.817 versus Snorkel's 0.822 for three categories, and 0.774 and 0.772 versus 0.770 for the full taxonomy, with neither student significantly outperforming Snorkel.

labels.label: challenges
labels.condition: Pretrained transformer students (BERT-base, xtremedistil) fine-tuned on full query+URL Snorkel labels with query+URL input, for both the three-category and the full taxonomy
labels.reason: Tables 7–8 give .826/.817 versus .822 and .774/.772 versus .770; Section 7.2 explicitly states no significant outperformance. The state rules classify such differences as absent.

relation.reason: Directly compares models trained on weak labels with their labeller on the same human-annotated evaluation set.

tranche.reason: Tests student performance against its weak supervisor in a new setting: query-intent classification using rule-based Snorkel labels.

source_check.notes: The supervisor aggregates heuristic rules rather than being a smaller pretrained model; no gold-trained strong ceiling or PGR is reported. Absent states rely on the authors' significance statement; Tables 7–8 provide no uncertainty estimates.

statements.correction: Three-category macro F1: BERT .826, xtremedistil .817, Snorkel .822. Full-taxonomy macro F1: BERT .774, xtremedistil .772, Snorkel .770. Section 7.2: no benchmark model significantly outperforms Snorkel with query+URL inputs.
statements.problem: The opening assertion that the student stays at or below its labeller is numerically inaccurate for BERT; the reported numbers and absence of significant outperformance are correct.
